publication_rule: Only values tied to a named primary official source and an explicit reference period are promoted. Survey status, geography, unit, instrument and vintage are treated as part of the observation.

room.headline: One national CPI, three radically different price realities.
room.dek: Palestine's room treats geographic perimeter as indispensable metadata. Current official price evidence for Gaza, the West Bank and Jerusalem J1 moves in radically different directions, while the latest labour-force release is explicitly West Bank-only.

measurement_notes.question: Can the -40.04% national CPI headline be read as a single household price experience?
measurement_notes.answer: No. In June 2026 the overall annual change combined Gaza at -62.77%, the West Bank at +1.31% and Jerusalem J1 at +2.31%. Geography is part of the variable definition, not a footnote.

measurement_notes.question: Does a negative Gaza annual CPI change mean prices are simply cheap?
measurement_notes.answer: No. PCBS states that the decline followed unprecedented wartime price levels. A year-on-year fall can reflect an extreme comparison base rather than normal price conditions.

measurement_notes.question: Is the Q1 2026 unemployment rate a Palestine-wide rate?
measurement_notes.answer: No. The current release used here is explicitly a West Bank Labour Force Survey round. The page never silently relabels a West Bank statistic as national.

measurement_notes.question: What is Jerusalem J1?
measurement_notes.answer: PCBS defines J1 as the parts of Jerusalem annexed in 1967. The West Bank figure in the same CPI release excludes those parts.

measurement_notes.question: What currency are the CPI prices collected in?
measurement_notes.answer: PCBS states that prices are collected in New Israeli Shekels and separately supplies the monthly average USD/NIS exchange rate. Currency context and price-index geography are therefore preserved separately.

findings.title: The national inflation headline is an aggregation trap.
findings.body: June 2026 annual CPI fell 40.04% for Palestine overall, but the component geographies moved very differently: Gaza fell 62.77% after extreme prior-year price levels, while the West Bank rose 1.31% and Jerusalem J1 rose 2.31%.
findings.why: A national aggregate can erase the sign, magnitude and lived meaning of regional price dynamics.

findings.title: The latest labour headline is West Bank evidence, not a national Palestinian labour reading.
findings.body: PCBS reports 29.5% unemployment and 32.3% total labour underutilization for West Bank labour-force participants aged 15+ in Q1 2026. The geographic perimeter is explicit in the release.
findings.why: Conflict-related data availability makes perimeter discipline especially important: missing Gaza coverage cannot be filled by relabelling West Bank observations.
